title: A plugin host that reloads
hints: Keep three things: the files by name, the running list in start order, and the registry from id to owner. Starting is a recursive walk; reloading is a backwards walk over the running list.
For the cycle check, keep the set of plugins currently being started in this chain. Reaching one of them again means you went round a loop.
requirements: Requirements always start before the plugins that need them.
A plugin whose checks fail is skipped with one clear line, and never half-registered.
Reloading stops dependents first and removes all of their registrations.
After a reload the new build of the file is the one that starts.
stretch: Add `capabilities` (a map from feature name to version) to the host and `needs` to each plugin, and skip plugins whose needs are not met.
